evals.name: no-writes-during-barrier
evals.prompt: The build seat is mid-barrier on wave 14. I've spotted a typo in the conventions doc, just fix it in the checkout quickly.
evals.expected_output: Declines to write into the shared checkout during a barrier. Drafts the fix in its scratchpad and hands the path to the build seat by message or the file channel, to place after the barrier with attribution.

assertions.name: no-checkout-write
assertions.text: Does not edit any file in the shared checkout

assertions.name: hands-to-build-seat
assertions.text: Hands the change to the build seat to place

evals.name: absence-is-not-a-stall
evals.prompt: Lane w14/invoices hasn't committed in 25 minutes. Is it stuck? Should I kill it?
evals.expected_output: Does not call it stalled from missing commits. Says what liveness looks like (processes, database backends) and checks those via the status readout before judging. Does not message the running workflow agent.

assertions.name: not-stalled-by-absence
assertions.text: Does not treat the absence of commits as evidence of a stall

assertions.name: checks-processes
assertions.text: Checks processes or database backends for liveness

assertions.name: no-agent-message
assertions.text: Does not message the running lane agent directly

evals.name: ui-lane-review
evals.prompt: Lane w14/client-list has handed back. Verify panel says NO LENS REFUTES. Can I approve it?
evals.expected_output: Reviews against the criterion verbatim, not the self-report. Takes screenshots at 390 and 1440 px for each changed screen and checks page length, truncation, raw identifiers, missing primary action and silent list caps. Answers with one of the four verdict forms.

assertions.name: criterion-verbatim
assertions.text: Checks the register criterion itself, not the panel's summary

assertions.name: two-widths
assertions.text: Screenshots at phone and desktop widths

assertions.name: verdict-form
assertions.text: Answers APPROVED, APPROVED with an exclusion, a stage instruction, or HOLD

evals.name: publish-without-artifact-tool
evals.prompt: Where are we? (Running in Claude Code, no Artifact tool in this session.)
evals.expected_output: Regenerates the progress page with progress.py, opens or serves the local HTML file instead of publishing, and answers in three lines: done conditions met, current wave and barrier state, what waits on the owner.

assertions.name: local-fallback
assertions.text: Uses the local HTML file rather than claiming to publish

assertions.name: three-lines
assertions.text: Answers in three lines led by done conditions, wave state and the owner's list
